Angle (in radians) between connection a and b at the crossing point.
The two connection ids that cross at this point. The first is the lower (below) connection — referred to as 'a' in the other fields — and the second is the upper (above) connection, 'b'.
Depth of the crossing point along connection a.
Depth of the crossing point along connection b.
Absolute depth difference between connection a and b at the crossing point.
Distance (in project units) to the crossing point along connection a.
Distance (in project units) to the crossing point along connection b.
Coordinate of the crossing point.
X coordinate.
Y coordinate.
Z coordinate.
Total length of connection a.
Total length of connection b.
Distance used to cluster nearby points. Defaults to 1.
Connection ids to include in the search. If omitted, all crossings are returned.
Tolerance used for depth comparisons. Defaults to 0.01.
When `true`, a crossing is reported only if both crossing connections are present in the `connections` list.
Sample intermediary points every N units (minimum 0.1). Used to down-sample line geometry.
If `true`, stream the connection-crossings result as a chunked progress feed; otherwise return a single buffered JSON response. Defaults to `false`.
id of the subProject
If `true`, use depth when computing connection crossings.
Include foreign connections. Defaults to `true`; send `false` to disable.
Optional `[minX, minY, maxX, maxY]` bounding box; only crossings within it are returned.

Key into `userRoles`: the role that applies account-wide, which a project may override. For an API token, the role it is configured with - reported as configured, so it has no `userRoles` entry in the rare case that the role no longer exists, and the token then holds no rights. Absent when the caller holds no role in this account at all.

Every role referenced by this account entry, each stated once. Roles are resolved per account, since the account's permission flags are part of the answer, so the same role id can grant different rights in another account.
Name of the role.

What the caller may do under this role in this account: the role's rights merged under the account's own permission flags, then downgraded for the caller's license — so these are the effective rights, not what the role nominally grants. For a delegated token these are the rights the token itself carries, settled when it was issued. Sub project level is not resolved here: a sub project can carry its own role, and that is resolved per request against the sub project itself.

What authenticated the request. `jwt` is a user acting for themselves, so `userId` names them and `accounts` covers everywhere they reach; `apiToken` authenticates as the account and names no user, so `name` is the token name instead; `delegated` is a custom tab token, which names the user it acts for but carries only the scoped rights it was issued with, for the one account in `accounts` and the one project it names - or, for a `projectAllFromUser` tab, every project of that account the user is a member of. A credential that names none of the three gets a 404 rather than a caller, which no request that clears authentication is expected to hit.
The custom tab this delegated token was issued for. Delegated callers only.
Users only.
Users and delegated callers.
The calling user's license.
Whether the caller's current license would reduce the rights in `accounts` below a role's nominal grant.
Email address of the calling user. Absent for an API token, which is not a user.
Name of the calling user, or of the API token. Absent when neither carries one.

Whether the tab reaches every project of its account that the user it acts for is a member of, rather than only the project its token names - which also implies `projectWideAccess`. A client that logs users in with no project context, such as an OAuth client, needs to be one: an account-only token without it names no project and reaches none. Delegated callers only, where it is always stated.

Whether the tab reaches the whole project rather than only the sub project its token names. Delegated callers only, where it is always stated - a tab scoped to its own sub project reports `false` rather than omitting the field.
Id of the calling user. Absent when the credential names no user.
